name: AWS Berwick

timeline.event: [AWS](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1622536/000162828025023501/tln-20250331.htm) acquires the Cumulus/Talen building campus for $650M.

Building 1 fit out and related construction begins under Amazon, based on the [Susquehanna River Basin Commission](https://www.srbc.gov/waav/search/GetPending?documentType=Application&isABRe=false&projectNumber=2024-056) (SRBC) schedule.

Building 1 operational estimate. According to [Google Earth Satellite Imagery](https://earth.google.com/web/search/Berwick,+PA/@41.08459175,-76.14321499,203.05778839a,756.59305105d,35y,0h,0t,0r/data=CiwiJgokCYCDFkPTLDRAEX6DFkPTLDTAGUGoL_2-p

Building 2 operational estimate. This is based on the progress visible in the September 2025 image. [The DEP](https://www.pacodeandbulletin.gov/secure/pabulletin/data/vol56/56-4/56-4.pdf) also issues an air plan approval to add 48 more emer

[The SRBC](https://www.srbc.gov/waav/Search/getdocket?documenttype=Approval&isabre=False&projectnumber=20260301) increases approved water use from 0.060 MGD to 0.129 MGD. This supports that some expansion is happening, but does not explicit

Buildings 1 and 2 visibly complete and operational. Building 3 appears complete and may be commissioning, but it's likely not operational yet given the immediate surrounding construction work. Several additional building shells and pads are

Building 3 expected to come online sometime around August 2026, since in the May satellite image it appeared structurally complete with minimal construction surrounding it. Basing MW estimate using Building 2 as a reference.
Building 4 expected to come online around August 2027, judging from prior satellite imagery. Modeled at twice Building 2's capacity because Building 4 is approximately twice its size.

sources.publisher: Epoch AI, Frontier Data Centers Hub (CC-BY)
sources.quote: AWS Berwick: current power 108 MW; owner Amazon.

explain: AWS Berwick is an operating AI data center in Berwick, PA, owned by amazon. Epoch AI estimates it draws 108 MW today and 212 MW when finished.
